Good morning. President Trump has[started his tour of Asia](https://www.nytimes.com/live/2026/11/17/world/trump-asean-summit) in the Philippines — where he was[very late to a diplomatic summit](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/17/world/asia/trump-manila-asean-late.html) . Leaked files show how Deutsche Bank, one of the world’s largest, has[protected Russian oligarchs](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/17/world/europe/deutsche-bank-russia-oligarchs-leaked-documents.html) . And we’ve got some reader thoughts about the new James Bond.


I’m going to start, though, with a few stories that caught my eye.

## Born sick


More than a dozen babies in the United States have been born infected with measles over the last two years, my colleague Teddy Rosenbluth reports.


Cases like those had been exceedingly rare. But measles is surging, and a new study shows that 112 pregnant women have been infected during the resurgence, most of whom were unvaccinated. Nearly a quarter went into the hospital with complications unrelated to their labor, including pneumonia and respiratory failure. One ended up in intensive care. Some delivered preterm. Two lost their pregnancies.


This fall, the C.D.C.[stopped](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/16/well/measles-pregnancy-newborns.html) ****[its scientists from sending out an urgent alert](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/16/well/measles-pregnancy-newborns.html) on measles in pregnancy, The Washington Post reported. After that, the researchers published their findings in The New England Journal of Medicine Evidence, rather than in the agency’s own scientific journal.


There have already been more than 5,000 cases nationwide in the United States this year, with 10 deaths. Today, international health officials plan to announce that the United States has lost its “measles elimination status.” That’s a big reversal. And if the effort to wipe out measles the first time is any lesson, it could take[many years to get it back](https://www.nytimes.com/2026/11/15/well/us-measles-elimination.html) .
